item.title: ESPN announcer Mike Breen apologizes after LeBron James refutes on-air story about him and Joel Embiid
item.description: LeBron James pushed back on Mike Breen's story about him and Joel Embiid on social media.
item.content:encoded:
Longtime ESPN NBA play-by-play announcer Mike Breen apologized Wednesday over a story he shared about LeBron James and Joel Embiid during a preseason game between the New York Knicks and Philadelphia 76ers earlier this week. 

The story, which Breen said on the air during the fourth quarter, was refuted on social media by James. 

"I'm so disappointed how the story was interpreted," Breen told ESPN. "The whole intent was praising LeBron for already having an impact on the team's professionalism and accountability, even something so benign as a player getting on the court for practice a minute or two late."

item.title: NBA Europe plans continue after EuroLeague rejects merger
item.description: The NBA is forging ahead with its proposed NBA Europe league. A key vote to merge with the EuroLeague just went down.
item.content:encoded:
As the NBA continues to pursue its expansion into Europe, the existing legacy league rejected a formal merger offer earlier this week.

Yet, that isn’t halting any plans for NBA Europe to forge ahead.

Membership groups from EuroLeague, which has been operating in the region since 1958, rejected a merger offer from the NBA that would have lumped operations under the proposed NBA Europe umbrella, a person with direct knowledge of the matter confirmed to USA TODAY Sports.

Despite that, talks are expected to continue as the NBA works toward a collaborative approach with EuroLeague.

The person spoke under the condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the negotiations, which have not been made public.

Yet, despite the failed merger offer, the NBA will not pause its plan to create the new, 14-to-16-team NBA Europe league across a dozen cities in Europe, some of which do not have permanent EuroLeague teams in place.

NBA plans for Europe: League format

The NBA has maintained that its NBA Europe plan will be a European basketball franchise for European fans, and that its structure would align closely with existing European sports infrastructure.

item.title: Dana Altman's retirement in offseason's twilight becomes latest in mysterious trend
item.description: Dana Altman became the latest high-profile college basketball coach to retire right before the start of the season. Is this an issue for the sport?
item.content:encoded:
Roughly 24 hours before he and his Oregon men’s basketball players were set to speak at Big Ten media days in Rosemont, Illinois, Dana Altman decided that after nearly 40 years as a Division I head coach, it was time to call it a career.

The longtime Ducks coach retired effective immediately on Wednesday, Oct. 7, only 26 days before they tip off their 2026-27 season against Montana.

The fact that the news is only so stunning says quite a bit about where college basketball finds itself in 2026.

item.title: Will Tony Stubblefield be Oregon's next coach? What to know of interim, longtime assistant
item.description: Is Tony Stubblefield a candidate for Oregon's head coach opening? Here's what to know of the interim coach after Dana Altman's retirement:
item.content:encoded:
Longtime Oregon men's basketball coach Dana Altman announced his retirement from coaching on Wednesday, Oct. 7, less than a month from the Ducks' season opener against Montana on Nov. 2.

Assistant coach Tony Stubblefield will serve as the interim coach, per the announcement. Prior to his second stint as an assistant under Altman in Oregon, Stubblefield was most recently the head coach at DePaul, accumulating a 28-54 record in three seasons with the Demons before he was fired.

item.title: Cole Swider has worked ‘really hard’ on body, defense since last stint with Lakers
item.description: The well-traveled wing has focused on improving his body and shooting versatility
item.content:encoded:
Four years ago, Cole Swider made his NBA debut for the Los Angeles Lakers, where he played seven games before bouncing across the Miami Heat, Detroit Pistons and Toronto Raptors for brief spells in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Last year, he spent the season in Europe playing for Anadolu Efes, making 51 combined appearances between EuroLeague and the Turkish Super League.

Now, he’s back with the Lakers on an Exhibit 10 contract and is eager to show how much he’s improved in numerous ways.
